zzz.zoomquilt.org.title: The Zoomquilt — the infinitely zooming painting
zzz.zoomquilt.org.what_it_is: The Zoomquilt — 'a collaborative infinitely zooming painting,' created in 2004 by Nikolaus Baumgarten with a collective of artists. It's the 'infinite zoom painting' from Jonas's list and one of the oldest icons of the creative web.
zzz.zoomquilt.org.how_its_designed: Pure content-forward — the painting is the design. Chrome is minimal: from getComputedStyle the stage is black (body rgb(0,0,0)) with grey helper text (rgb(170,170,170)) in a Helvetica/Arial system stack, and the 'About' heading in Open Sans at 40px in a signature orange-red (rgb(255,82,25)). There's no CSS design system or custom properties — it predates them; the loaded Google Sans webfonts come from the AdSense frame, not the artwork.
zzz.zoomquilt.org.palette: A black stage (rgb(0,0,0)) with grey UI text (rgb(170,170,170)) and an orange-red heading accent (rgb(255,82,25)); all real colour lives in the painted artwork.
zzz.zoomquilt.org.fonts: Open Sans for the 'About' heading (40px) and a Helvetica/Arial system stack for body text; Google Sans is present only via the ad frame.

essence.subject: The Zoomquilt, a collaborative infinitely zooming painting made in 2004 by Nikolaus Baumgarten with a collective of artists
essence.does: Shows a seamless, endless zoom through a surreal hand-painted world of alpine meadows, mountains, trees, orange tendrils and caverns. Each scene dissolves into the next in a continuous loop. Viewers control the zoom with the up and down keys, and an about panel credits the participating artists.
essence.for_whom: Anyone interested in digital art, creative-web history and surreal visual experiences
